newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: French express companies lose case against post office.
newsitem.headline: French express companies lose case against post office.

text.p: Private express mail companies in France lost a court battle on Wednesday to force the European Commission to investigate their complaint against the French post office.

The European Court of First Instance upheld a Commission decision to reject a 1990 complaint filed by French express delivery association SFEI about the relationship between La Poste and its international express mail subsidiary SFMI.
SFEI and three French-based companies -- DHL, Service CRIE and May Courier -- charged that logistical and commercial support provided by La Poste violated European Union competition rules.
But the Commission refused to investigate, saying the companies had not offered enough evidence that the alleged abuse would continue.

It said it had addressed the potential problems raised by the companies in a 1993 policy document on EU postal services and in a 1991 decision setting conditions on an international express mail joint venture involving La Poste.
That decision required La Poste to offer both SFMI and other express operators similar access to its facilities.
The court agreed with the Commission's reasoning, saying it was not obliged to probe past abuses that did not have EU interest.
The Commission opened a separate investigation last April into SFEI's complaint that France had provided illegal subsidies to SFMI.
The European Court of Justice handed SFEI a victory in July when it ruled that the French government may have provided illegal subsidies for express mail services.

It said logistical support including personnel, vehicles, buildings and marketing campaigns could be considered state aid if the post office charged less for the services than under "normal market conditions".
If that were the case and France had not cleared the aid with the Commission, a French court could order the money paid back, it said. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
